## 1. Exact literal inputs and the new consumer

Fix the original prime p congruent to 13 or 19 modulo 24, the complete unramified DVR O with perfect residue field, Witt automorphism sigma, and fraction field K=O[1/p]. O is an INTEGRAL DOMAIN and DVR, not a field. Put

 S=4r^3-3r, f=1-r^2, q=4r^2-1, P=fq,
 D=(2P)^-1 [[2S-1,1],[4S-5,-(2S-1)]],
 R0=O[r,f^-1,q^-1]^dagger, R=R0[1/p],
 L_D(h)=h'+hD.

Rows, the global coordinate r, and the oneform dr are fixed. All new maps below are R0-linear horizontal maps of finite free modules with connection. The differential itself is O-linear. Neither the lattice nor D is varied with n.

 c_n=[b_n dr] in C_int=R0^(1x2)dr/L_D(R0^(1x2))dr

The primitive v_n is unique and has least p-denominator n. It also computes the full integral horizontal End and Aut of each lattice. This uses the new torsion data; its classes are all ZERO after inverting p, so the old nonzero K-projective source-class classification does not distinguish them.

No source, independent technical whole or ordinary acceptance of this new appendix exists at its creation. Old accepted inputs are reused as actual mathematical premises, not as votes on this new consumer.

## 2. Integral preliminaries and constants

The actual R0 embeds in R. One can see the needed p-torsionfreeness directly without replacing the weak ring by a strong completion. Let A0=O[r,f^-1,q^-1]. It is p-torsionfree. Its p-adic completion is also p-torsionfree: if px=0, a representative a of x modulo p^(m+1) has pa in p^(m+1)A0. Cancelling p in A0 gives a in p^m A0. Thus x vanishes modulo every p^m, hence is zero in the separated inverse limit. The integral weak completion is the specified weak-presentation subring of that completion, so it is p-torsionfree and injects into its p-localization R. This is only an injection argument, not permission to use arbitrary strongly completed coefficients.

The second input's actual infinity coefficient bridge says that an element of R0 has integral Laurent coefficients on the original infinity annulus. A constant a in R0 intersect K therefore has its constant Laurent coefficient a in O. Conversely O is contained in R0. Thus

 R0 intersect K = O.                                           (3)

It follows from (1) and (3) that the constants of R0 are exactly O. Likewise any scalar horizontal endomorphism matrix over R0 has its scalar in O. No nonzero element of O is automatically declared a unit: O^* will be required separately for isomorphisms.

For each c_n in (2),

 ann_O(c_n)=p^n O.                                             (4)

Indeed every nonzero a in O is p^j times a unit. If j<n and a killed c_n, multiplying the equality by a suitable unit and p^(n-1-j) would contradict p^(n-1)c_n!=0. If j>=n it kills c_n, and zero belongs to the annihilator as well.

## 3. Actual integral carriers and their common weak split realization

For each n>=1 define N_n=R0^(1x3) with

 nabla_n(h,a)=(L_D(h)+a b_n,a')dr,
 D_n=[[D,0],[b_n,0]].                                         (5)

Let M0=R0^(1x2) with the original connection. The literal maps
i(h)=(h,0) and q_n(h,a)=a are horizontal and give

 0 -> M0 -> N_n -> 1 -> 0,                                    (6)

where 1 is the fixed trivial rank1 connection over R0. All modules, matrices and maps are in the declared actual ring.

A horizontal integral section of q_n is a row (h,1) with L_D(h)=-b_n. Its existence would make c_n zero. Since n>=1 and c_n has exact order p^n, the sequence (6) does not split integrally.

Over R define the explicit matrix

 W_n=[[I2,0],[v_n,1]]: N_n tensor R -> N_0 tensor R,            (7)

where N_0 denotes the same construction with b=0, hence M0 directsum 1. In the row convention a right matrix W from a source connection D_b to a target D_c is horizontal iff W'=D_b W-WD_c. Its lower-left equation in (7) is exactly L_D(v_n)=b_n. Therefore W_n is horizontal. Its actual two-sided inverse is [[I2,0],[-v_n,1]], which is also horizontal by direct multiplication and the reverse equation. Hence every N_n tensor R is the SAME split object M directsum 1, with an actual displayed weak isomorphism. It is not an assertion that a K-vector extension class alone supplies an integral isomorphism.

## 4. Unrestricted integral comparisons automatically preserve the kernel

We first determine every R0-linear horizontal functional N_n -> 1. Write its column as (u,t), with u in R0^2 and t in R0. Horizontality gives

 u'=Du, t'=b_n u.

After embedding R0 in R, (1) forces u=0. Then t'=0 and (3) gives t in O. Conversely each t q_n is horizontal. Consequently

 Hom_(R0,nabla)(N_n,1)=O q_n.                                (8)

The COMMON kernel of these functionals is i(M0), since q_n itself is in (8). We do not use the false integral assertion that every nonzero multiple t q_n is surjective; for t divisible by p it need not be.

Now let W:N_n->N_m be ANY R0-linear horizontal comparison, without a pre-imposed filtered category. The functional q_m composed with W lies in (8). Thus W automatically sends i(M0) into i(M0), and its last column is (0,0,beta)^T for beta in O.

Write its upper-left block as A. Its horizontal equation is A'=DA-AD. Applying (1) over R and then (3), A=alpha I2 with alpha in O. Thus every comparison necessarily has the form

 W=[[alpha I2,0],[t,beta]], alpha,beta in O,
 L_D(t)=alpha b_n-beta b_m.                                  (9)

Conversely (9) substituted into W'=D_n W-WD_m proves horizontality. The row t, if it exists, is unique because ker L_D=0 over R. By the definition of the integral O-module cokernel, existence is equivalent to

 alpha c_n = beta c_m in C_int.                              (10)

Equations (9)-(10) concern actual integral rows. No integration in an enlarged completion or fractional solution is silently substituted for t in R0.

## 5. Pairwise integral nonisomorphism with a fixed weak realization

If W is an integral horizontal isomorphism, its inverse is horizontal and has the same block form by section 4. Let its corresponding scalars be alpha',beta' in O. Multiplication in both directions yields

 alpha alpha'=1, beta beta'=1.

Thus alpha,beta are in O^*, not merely nonzero elements of K. Equation (10) and unit multiplication preserve exact p-power order in C_int. Since c_n and c_m have orders p^n and p^m, respectively, an isomorphism forces n=m.

Conversely n=m has the identity isomorphism. We have proved

 N_n is R0-horizontal-isomorphic to N_m iff n=m.              (11)

This covers all horizontal GL3(R0) matrices, because kernel preservation was proved for every comparison rather than imposed as a category restriction. By (7), all these pairwise distinct integral lattices have one and the same split weak realization after p is inverted. The indexing n is not a change of prime, coefficient field, lattice definition or connection D.

## 6. Full actual End, Aut and integral indecomposability

For m=n, condition (10) is (alpha-beta)c_n=0. By (4), alpha-beta belongs to p^n O. Every endomorphism is therefore exactly

 E_n(alpha,beta)=
 [[alpha I2,0],[((alpha-beta)/p^n)u_n,beta]],
 alpha,beta in O, alpha congruent beta modulo p^n.            (12)

This formula genuinely lies in R0 and is horizontal by (2). Necessity follows from (9)-(10), and uniqueness of its lower row follows from kernel-zero. It includes the zero map and all nonunits, not only automorphisms.

The actual matrix product satisfies
E_n(alpha,beta) E_n(alpha',beta')=E_n(alpha alpha',beta beta').
The lower-row coefficient identity is

 ((alpha-beta)alpha'+beta(alpha'-beta'))/p^n
       =(alpha alpha'-beta beta')/p^n.

Consequently there is a full O-algebra identification

 End_(R0,nabla)(N_n)
   = { (alpha,beta) in O x O : alpha=beta modulo p^n },       (13)

with coordinatewise multiplication, represented by the actual matrices (12). It is the indicated fiber-product order in K x K. No classification of an unrelated operator or strong-ring endomorphism algebra is claimed.

Its automorphisms are precisely

 Aut_(R0,nabla)(N_n)
   = { (alpha,beta) in O^* x O^* : alpha=beta modulo p^n }.   (14)

Necessity of both units was proved with the inverse, not with a determinant-nonzero argument. For sufficiency, the actual two-sided block inverse has lower row -((alpha-beta)/p^n)u_n/(alpha beta). This is integral and equals the lower row in E_n(alpha^-1,beta^-1), since alpha^-1-beta^-1 is still divisible by p^n.

Finally an idempotent in (13) has alpha^2=alpha and beta^2=beta. O is a DVR INTEGRAL DOMAIN, so alpha,beta are individually 0 or 1. Since n>=1, congruence modulo p^n excludes (0,1) and (1,0). The only idempotents are 0 and I.

Any nontrivial horizontal direct-sum decomposition over R0, even one whose summands are merely finite projective rather than given in advance as free blocks, supplies a nontrivial R0-linear horizontal projection. Such an idempotent does not exist. Therefore each N_n is integrally indecomposable as a connection, although its underlying module is free and its weak realization is explicitly split. After p is inverted, (13) becomes K x K, consistently with that split realization. This does not use scalar End as a surrogate for irreducibility.
